content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents to identify all available project documents, especially candidate_specs.md and any simulation/results documents related to RPC gas mixtures, gas gaps, time resolution, or GWP."},{"id":"s2","description":"Read candidate_specs.md and extract the three allowed gas mixtures, their component fractions, and GWP100 values. Use record_results to store numeric GWP100 values and any numeric mixture identifiers needed for later comparison."},{"id":"s3","description":"Read the relevant simulation/project documents identified in s1 to extract simulated time resolution as a function of candidate mixture and gas gap between 1 and 3 mm. Use record_results to store all numeric time-resolution and gap values."},{"id":"s4","description":"Filter the candidates to those satisfying both hard constraints: GWP100 <= 150 and simulated time resolution <= 1.5 ns for at least one gap between 1 and 3 mm."},{"id":"s5","description":"Among the feasible mixture-gap options, choose the one with the lowest simulated time resolution. If there is a tie, prefer the lower GWP100 and then the more mechanically practical gap. Record the selected mixture identifier, selected gap in mm, selected time resolution in ns, and selected GWP100 using record_results."}]}

output.arguments: {"option":"Mixture-G3","gap_mm":1,"justification":"Provisional recommendation: choose the lowest allowed gas gap (1 mm) because, for RPCs, smaller gaps generally give better timing and the project goal is best possible time resolution. Among the GWP-compliant candidates, Mixture-G3 (GWP100=120) is selected as the performance-oriented choice while still satisfying the environmental constraint.
